disease_label_per_paper: Stevens-Johnson syndrome/toxic epidermal necrolysis in an orthotopic liver transplant recipient
presentation_summary: 48-year-old woman developed SJS/TEN after orthotopic liver transplant performed for secondary biliary cirrhosis with portal hypertension and recurrent cholangitis.
Initial post-transplant course was normal, but she developed new portal vein thrombosis 2 weeks after transplant requiring endovascular stenting.
One month after transplant she developed worsening fevers; CT showed pneumoperitoneum concerning for perforation, and exploratory laparotomy found purulence but no perforation.

During the operation she developed a maculopapular rash and bullae across the chest and torso with persistent fevers to 103 F and new pancytopenia: WBC fell from 10.1 to 0.3 x10^9/L and platelets from 237 to 47 x10^9/L.
Course progressed to extensive bullae on torso and extremities with oral mucosal sloughing and diarrhea; skin and mucosal sloughing resolved after 2-3 weeks of treatment.

clinical_course.event: Orthotopic liver transplant performed for secondary biliary cirrhosis, portal hypertension, and recurrent cholangitis.
New portal vein thrombosis identified 2 weeks post-transplant and managed by endovascular stenting through trans-splenic access.
Worsening fevers and CT pneumoperitoneum concern prompted exploratory laparotomy; purulence was seen without perforation; maculopapular rash and bullae began across chest and torso with pancytopenia.
Skin biopsy obtained with concern for SJS or graft-versus-host disease; HLA testing argued against GVHD.

After stopping suspected medications and treatment with filgrastim, steroids, IVIG, infliximab, cyclosporine transition, and wound care, pancytopenia and skin/mucosal sloughing resolved over 2-3 weeks.
Hospitalization lasted 4 months because of persistent intra-abdominal infection; later discharged doing well with functioning graft and resolved infections.
